title: No Work Today, Mii's Got You
amb: phone alarm buzzing, soft rustle of a duvet, morning birds outside the window, tiny paws on a wool rug, plate and jam jar lid clinking on a wooden counter

lines.text: Bzzz. Bzzz. Your phone alarm buzzes on the nightstand, for the second time. You fumble for it, press it quiet, and sink back under the duvet.
Then something small lands on the blanket. It's as light as a bread roll. Four soft steps climb toward your chest.
A round paw presses down on the corner of your duvet. It's pinning it, very firmly.
No work today. Mii will take care of you.
You open one eye. It's Mii, your three-month-old orange kitten, in its cream linen bib with the little blue fish on the pocket. Its whiskers twitch. It is trying very hard to look serious.
You blink at the ceiling. Then it comes back to you.
"Oh, right," you mumble. "It's my day off. I forgot the alarm."
Mii heard it. Two times. Too loud.
So today, Mii is in charge.
You reach out and rub the top of its head with one finger. Its ears flatten, then spring right back up.
You stay. Mii does everything.
It hops off the bed and lands with a soft thump on the rug. Then comes a scuffing sound, back and forth, back and forth. Something is being pushed across the floor, slowly and with great effort.
Slippers. For you.
You sit up and look down. Your slippers wait neatly beside the bed, toes pointing at the mattress and heels facing out. They're backwards.
You tell Mii, gently, that they're the wrong way round.
Mii knew. Not on purpose.
Round two.
It butts one slipper with its forehead until the slipper swings around, then does the other. You slide your feet in. They're warm, because Mii was lying on them.
Pad, pad, pad. It leads you to the kitchen with its tail straight up like a little flag.

The wooden counter is cool under your palms. A slice of bread already sits on a plate, slightly crooked. Next to it is a jar of apricot jam with a loose lid, and the handle of a small spoon peeks out from under the lid.
Breakfast. Mii makes it. You sit.
Mii stands up on its back legs, tucks its head under the lid, and pushes. The lid wobbles, tips, and clacks onto the counter, spinning.
Open. Easy.
The smell is sweet and sunny. Mii taps the spoon handle. The spoon tips, and a bright blob of jam plops onto the bread.
Then, to spread it, Mii pats it. Pat. Pat.
It lifts its paw. Right in the middle of your toast is one perfect paw print, four little toe beans and a pad pressed into apricot jam.
That is the decoration.
It licks its sticky paw with its tiny tongue going fast. Its ears dip, just a little.
A laugh slips out of you before you can stop it.
Good laugh? Okay. You eat. Mii watches.
You lean toward the plate. Then something crinkles, papery and soft. It's coming from the bib pocket, which is round and full, as if it was packed ahead of time.
Your eyes drift to it. Instantly, both of Mii's paws fly up and cover the little blue fish. It sits very, very straight.
[whispering] Not for you. Not yet.
It doesn't look away. Under its paws, the pocket rustles again. Whatever is in there, Mii brought it to your bed this morning on purpose.

prompt: Your paw-print toast is waiting, and Mii is guarding that rustling pocket with both paws. How do you respond to your little caretaker?
choices: I take a big bite right through the jam paw print.
I ask softly, "What's in your pocket, sweetheart?"
